document.title: The Harakat-ul-Ansar - The Pakistan Dimension [Excised] (Karachi 01617)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Haqqani History: Bin Ladin's Advocate Inside the Taliban
document.note: [Secret] Report on the Kashmiri militant group Harakat-ul-Ansar. Many of its activists are Afghan war veterans who fought with Maulana Jalaluddin Haqqani in Paktia. A significant portion of the membership is non-Pakistani, including veterans from Algeria, Tunisia, Sudan, Egypt and elsewhere. Three sources say the membership also includes a small number of American Muslims, with estimates ranging from six to sixteen.

persons.name: Jalauddin Haqqani
persons.role: Afghan mujahideen commander in Paktia; veterans who fought with him are reported among HuA activists, and former mujahideen associated with him reportedly conduct HuA training

mentions.quote: VETERANS OF THE AFGHAN WAR WHO FOUGHT ALONG WITH MAULANA JALAUDDIN HAQQANI IN PAK.TIA PROVINCE
BY FORMER AFGHAN MUJAHIDEEN; ASSOCIATED WITH MAULANA HAQQANI.

persons.name: Fazil ur-Rehman Khalil
persons.role: Reported leader of Harakat ul Ansar (per two sources)

mentions.quote: THE NAME GIVEN BY TWO SOURCES AS THE LEADER OF HARAKAT IS FAZIL UR-REHMAN KHALIL.
KHALIL, WHO IS EVIDENTLY FROM PUNJAB, REPORTEDLY CAME TO KARACHI IN THE AFTERMATH OF THE FEBRUARY 5 SHOOTINGS

persons.name: Maulana Farooq Kashmiri
persons.role: Named in other information as leader of HuA

mentions.quote: OTHER INFORMATION INDICATES THAT A MAULANA FAROOQ KASHMIRI IS THE LEADER OF HUA.

persons.name: Pir Wijahad Ali
persons.role: Pakistani pir in Rawalpindi reportedly with an American Muslim following, linked to HuA members

mentions.quote: SOURCE NAMED A PIR WIJAHAD ALI IN RAWALPINDI AS THE PIR WITH AN AMERICAN FOLLOWING.

organizations.name: Harakat ul Ansar
organizations.notes: Deobandi Sunni group, 2,000-10,000 activists; active in Kashmir since 1993 and kidnapped two British citizens in 1994; trains near Miran Shah; Feb 5 1995 Karachi fundraising; funded by private donors.

organizations.name: Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam (JUI/F)
organizations.notes: Reported sponsor of HuA, using it to gain political and financial support.

organizations.name: Sipah-e-Sahaba
organizations.notes: Linked to HuA; HuA called its foreign wing.

organizations.name: Tablighi Jamaat
organizations.notes: Non-political missionary organization from which HuA's original activists reportedly came; annual meeting at Raiwind.

events.description: Violence in Karachi killed 23; drive-by shooting of HuA fundraising pavilion in Liaquatabad.
Shooting of two U.S. Consulate employees in Karachi.
HuA kidnapped two British citizens in Indian-controlled Kashmir.
Karachi consulate cable on HuA sent to State Department.
Violence in Karachi killed 23 including a drive-by shooting on an HUA fundraising pavilion in Liaquatabad.
HUA organized five tented pavilions in Karachi to collect funds for Kashmir jihad.
Two U.S. Consulate employees shot in Karachi.
HUA kidnapped two British citizens in Indian-controlled Kashmir.
U.S. Consulate Karachi cable on HUA's Pakistan dimension sent.
Harakat ul Ansar reportedly first organized in Central Punjab to assist Afghan mujahideen.
Drive-by shootings in Karachi, with a Harakat fund-raising drive held the same day.
Fazil ur-Rehman Khalil came to Karachi after the Feb 5 shootings to offer condolences to victims' families.
A source told a US Consulate political officer that Harakat has publicly solicited donations in Pakistani cities before.
U.S. Consulate Karachi sends cable on Harakat ul Ansar's Pakistan dimension.

key_claims: HuA has 2,000-10,000 Deobandi activists, many Afghan war veterans who fought with Jalauddin Haqqani in Paktia.
HuA training camps near Miran Shah are run by former mujahideen associated with Haqqani.
HuA is sponsored by JUI/F and linked to SSP.
HuA is well-financed through private donations from Pakistan, Egypt, Algeria, Sudan and Gujarati Muslims in London.
Membership includes Arab/North African Afghan war veterans and a few American Muslims.
Sources saw no threat to the US from HuA.
